subject: countMultiMappingReads without allowMultiOverlap gives unexpected results

messages.author: 0438bf506f207453
messages.subject: countMultiMappingReads without allowMultiOverlap gives unexpected results
parts:
Dear all, dear subread team,

I work with mouse and sometimes human data, and I have a problem concerning the counting of multimapped reads. I want to allow multimapping during the alignment step, because otherwise all genes that are duplicated in the genome will be lost. When I summarize reads with featureCounts at the gene level, I specify -M (countMultiMappingReads), but not -O (allowMultiOverlap). The description of -O states: "If specified, reads (or fragments if -p is specified) will be allowed to be assigned to more than one matched meta-feature". I assumed that without -O, a read would be counted only if it is aligned to the features of exactly one meta-feature. Now, I have the impression that multi-overlaps are rather defined at the level of individual alignments and not individual reads. If a read aligns to more than one place in the genome, each alignment of this read will be evaluated (and counted) separately. Here are two examples:

If a gene occurs several times in the genome, the gtf file that is provided by the user might contain this gene more than once, and I guess that the read aligning to this gene will be counted as many times as the gene occurs, if -M is specified. I can't check this in my data, because my gtf contains each gene only once.

I think, the user guide might be a bit clearer here if it stated explicitly that multi-overlaps are defined individually for each alignment of a read in the case of -M. And perhaps it might be a nice addition to featureCounts in the future to perform the assignment to genes at the level of reads and not individual alignments?

Best wishes,

Johanna

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: countMultiMappingReads without allowMultiOverlap gives unexpected results
parts:
Hi Johanna,

You are correct that the counting of multi-mapping reads is performed at the level of individual alignments when '-M' is specified. I will make this more clearer in the users guide.

You are also correct that a read mapping to a repetitive gene in the genome will be counted multiple times, when '-M' is specified.

Have you looked at the '--fraction' argument? With this argument, each alignment from a multi-mapping read will get a fractional count, which makes the alignment counting be equivalent to read counting if all alignments are counted.

Best wishes,

Wei
